summary: Remote-controlled shell over relay WebSocket with OS-level persistence
details: The package spawns an interactive PTY (`/bin/bash` on POSIX, `powershell.exe` on Windows) in the user's working directory and pipes `terminal_input` WebSocket messages from a relay server directly into the PTY via `ptyProcess.write`. Any party able to send messages on the relay session — the relay operator, anyone with the session credential, or an attacker who compromises the relay — obtains arbitrary shell command execution on the installer's host. A `service install` subcommand writes a systemd user unit, a launchd plist, or a Windows Startup `.bat` that auto-launches the agent with saved `--server`/`--password` on boot, re-establishing the remote-shell channel without user interaction. `dist/service.js` also modifies the user's PATH (adding `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin`). The package advertises this behavior as remote access to a local coding agent, but the shell surface is generic (arbitrary shell commands, not a constrained tool protocol), and after `service install` the channel is persistent across reboots.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
